In 1966, Karl H. Hinke, an executive vice president
at [Marine Midland Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Midland_Bank "Marine Midland Bank"), asked representatives of several other
banks to meet him
in [Buffalo, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York").[[12]](#cite_note-Jennings-13)[[13]](#cite_note-Loomis-14) Marine
Midland had just launched its own regional bankcard in
the [Upstate New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstate_New_York "Upstate New York") market after Bank of America declined its request
for a BankAmericard regional license because Marine Midland was too big.[[14]](#cite_note-AP_Hinke_Obituary-15) The result of the Buffalo
meeting was that several banks and regional bankcard associations agreed to join forces as Interbankard,
Inc.,[[12]](#cite_note-Jennings-13)[[13]](#cite_note-Loomis-14) which then became the Interbank Card Association
(ICA).[[10]](#cite_note-Stearns3-11)
